messages:
Ethan: seeing a transient OOM on a subset of requests to model-x on pool-highmem. started ~10:04 UTC, correlates with a kernel-autotune pass + a shift in seq_len distribution (more 8k-ish inputs). logs show KV cache grew ~3x and allocator hit large contiguous free failure. stack: 
Ethan: `runtime: select_kernel=autotune -> fallback=vector32`, then immediate `cudaMalloc failed` and `OOM reclaim attempt`
Priya: ack — thanks for flagging. any deploys around that time?
Ethan: no user deploys. infra-bot reports autoscaler activity but no new instances. I captured a heap diff and perf counters. attaching short snippets below.
Ben: hmm autotune picked a kernel with larger workspace requirements for long sequences. if seq length shifted, autotuner stats might be stale. can you paste the profiler snippet?
Ethan: profiler: 
```
KVCacheSizeMB: baseline=120 -> peak=410
KernelChosen: fast32_complex (workspace=1.8GB)
AllocatorFreeBlocks: fragmented: yes
ContinuousFreeReq: 2.0GB -> fail
```

Priya: that kernel looks aggressive. two quick mitigations: 1) force kernel pin to `fast32_compact` (lower workspace), 2) enable aggressive KV eviction for affected route. both are safe short-term.
Aisha: agree. also flip on request-shaping on route: max_input_tokens=4096, prefix-truncation=true, and temporarily reduce batch_size for that route to 2. fallback policy: if mem_pressure>0.8 reject with 503 or route to smaller model.
Ben: concise commands:
```
rwdctl runtime set --pool=highmem --model=model-x kernel=fast32_compact
rwdctl route update /chat-x --kv-eviction=aggressive --max-batch=2
```

Priya: add circuit breaker config so we don't cascade:
```
{
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_inflight": 30,
    "max_latency_ms": 1200,
    "memory_pressure_threshold": 0.8,
    "fallback_model": "model-x-compact"
  }
}
```

Ethan: applied kernel pin and route updates at 10:12. memory back to baseline within ~45s. no more OOMs so far. rolling back autoscaler bump to check.
Aisha: please add an alert rule: if allocator_contiguous_failures > 0 for 3m then page eng-runtime oncall. and emit a metric for kernel_autotune_runs per minute so we can catch frequent reselection.
Priya: followup playbook we've been discussing, staged into quick-run checklist: 1) identify offending route and model, 2) pin kernel to compact variant, 3) enable KV eviction and reduce batch_size, 4) set per-route request shaping (max_input_tokens/prefix_truncation), 5) enable circuit breaker to fallback to compact model, 6) add alert for contiguous allocation failures + autotune storms, 7) post-incident: run autotune with updated seq_len hist (simulate 90th pct).
Ben: long-term: adapt kernel-autotune to weigh workspace variance and prefer compact kernels when KV cache growth is likely (e.g., high percent of long-prefixes). also consider opportunistic buffer reuse heuristics when fragmentation detected.
Ethan: saving artifacts to shared drive: /shared/eng-runtime/incident-1768450017/ with heapdiff, profiler, and commands executed. tagging @oncall for visibility.
infra-bot: deploy job `apply-kernel-pin` succeeded (job id 88421), route updates applied, alerts created. :white_check_mark:
Priya: good recovery. I'll formalize the mini-playbook and drop it into runbooks/ and link in the incident. everyone please add any missing immediate mitigations to the thread.
Aisha: added note — prefer soft-eviction first (age-based) before full KV purge; hard purge can cause quality regressions.
Ethan: noted. closing for now but keep watch on kernel_autotune_runs metric for next 24h. :eyes:
